newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democrats to stage Tiananmen protest.
newsitem.headline: HK democrats to stage Tiananmen protest.

text.p: Hong Kong's democracy movement won permission on Wednesday to commemorate China's 1989 anti-democracy crackdown, even though the rally would come close to the territory's July 1 handover to Beijing.

The Urban Council, in charge of Hong Kong's parks, gave a green light to the Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements in China to hold a rally on June 4 marking the crushing of student-led protests centred on Beijing's Tiananmen Square. But the Democratic Party, a strong critic of China's communist leaders, failed to secure a venue for a separate rally on June 30 to mark the end of 150-plus years of British rule.
The Alliance is a broad movement, with the Democratic Party as one of its core elements.

The June 4 rally has been an annual event in Hong Kong since 1989 when a million people poured onto the streets in solidarity with demonstrators in Beijing, whose democracy movement was crushed by Chinese tanks and soldiers with heavy loss of life.
Every year it has attracted tens of thousands of people.
The Alliance had feared it would lose out to a pro-China group, which planned to hold a soccer match on June 4 this year as part of pre-handover festivities.
Despite securing the venue this year, Alliance sources said it might be the last because China has announced plans to curb civil liberties in Hong Kong after the handover.
